lines.text: Every March and November, Americans scramble to change their clocks, except in two entire states.
Hawaii and almost all of Arizona refuse to observe Daylight Saving Time.
The federal Uniform Time Act of nineteen sixty-six allows states to opt out of moving clocks forward.
Hawaii sits close to the equator, where day length barely changes throughout the four seasons anyway.
In scorching Arizona, adding an extra hour of blistering sunlight in the hot evening is the last thing residents want.
Extra daylight in Phoenix means blasting expensive air conditioning an extra hour during summer heatwaves.
Would you prefer year-round permanent daylight time, or should we keep changing the clocks?
